items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Merrill Spepter was also there because Buck was engaged to play a ball in a hotel that night with a group lead by Glyn Pacque.

ctx.x: Other than the fact that we had no music on the stands, we still made a hit with the public at the Chikito. Later Norman Lester wrote some original tunes which actually had no swing possibilities and although he was a good piano man, he was not an arranger. But we played the tunes every night because I was a begger and had no choice.

"Willie the Lion" Smith came to Europe during this time and his tour brought him to Berne. There was a jam session every Saturday and Sunday afternoon at which I would invite the local musicians to participate and the joint would jump during these sessions. The first of December, Buck Clayton and George Johnson along with the "Lion" (who was giving recitals in Switzerland at the time), were invited to the session. I taken the occasion to ask "Buck" if he would make me some arrangements, but for some reason which I never found out why, he never did any for me and he was engaged through the influence of Felix to come to the Chikito quite a few times and play with my orchestra.
